seoTitle: BoJack Horseman Test: Which Character Are You? (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take the BoJack Horseman test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're BoJack, Princess Carolyn, Diane, Todd, Mr. Peanutbutter, Hollyhock or Judah — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the charming mess, the unstoppable fixer or the overthinker? Answer 12 everyday questions about work, friends and big decisions, and find out which BoJack Horseman character you are.

characters.name: BoJack
characters.title: The Charming Mess
characters.summary: Funny, sharp and secretly desperate to be liked. You want to be better, you just keep getting in your own way.
description: Like BoJack, you've got real charm. He was the star of the 1990s family sitcom Horsin' Around.
You chase the big win, hoping it'll finally fix how you feel. BoJack pinned his comeback on starring in the Secretariat movie.
You do try to change. BoJack went to rehab and later took a teaching job at Wesleyan.
characters.flaw: You put off the hard stuff, then wonder why it got harder.
characters.signature: A sad, funny one-liner and a phone call you keep putting off.
characters.clashReason: they'd cancel on you last minute, then make it about their own bad day

characters.name: Princess Carolyn
characters.title: The Fixer
characters.summary: Driven, capable and always three moves ahead. You can handle anything, except slowing down.
description: Like Princess Carolyn, you get things done. She worked as a talent agent before starting her own agency, VIM.
You don't quit when things fall apart. When VIM closed, she reopened it as a management company.
You want it all, and you'll fight for it. She adopted a baby porcupine, Ruthie, while still running her business.
characters.flaw: You take on everyone's problems and forget to look after yourself.
characters.signature: A packed calendar and a backup plan for your backup plan.
characters.clashReason: they'd turn your relaxing day off into a to-do list

characters.name: Diane
characters.title: The Overthinker
characters.summary: Thoughtful, principled and always asking what it all means. You'd rather be right than comfortable.
description: Like Diane, you think deeply about everything. She ghostwrote BoJack's memoir, One Trick Pony.
You want your work to matter. Diane wrote for the feminist blog Girl Croosh, and travelled to war-torn Cordovia hoping to help.
You find your own way in the end. After struggling with her memoir, she started a teen detective series, Ivy Tran: Food Court Detective.
characters.flaw: You can overthink a good thing until it stops feeling good.
characters.signature: A notebook full of half-finished essays and strong opinions.
characters.clashReason: they'd question every choice you make, out loud

characters.name: Todd
characters.title: The Free Spirit
characters.summary: Cheerful, kind and full of wonderfully strange ideas. Life happens to you, and you're mostly fine with it.
description: Like Todd, you go with the flow. He turned up at BoJack's house for a party and simply never left.
Your ideas are big and a little bit odd. Todd wrote a rock opera, and co-ran a Halloween store that was only open in January.
You're kinder than people expect. Todd ended up running a daycare in the VIM building.
characters.flaw: You start ten things and finish maybe one.
characters.signature: A wildly ambitious idea and absolutely no plan.
characters.clashReason: they'd drag you into a strange scheme and leave you to finish it

characters.name: Mr. Peanutbutter
characters.title: The Ray of Sunshine
characters.summary: Upbeat, friendly and up for anything. You say yes first and think about it later.
description: Like Mr. Peanutbutter, everyone seems to like you. He starred in his own sitcom, Mr. Peanutbutter's House.
You throw yourself into new things. He hosted a game show and even ran for Governor of California.
You stay positive, sometimes too positive. His cheerful, people-pleasing nature can make him miss what others are really feeling.
characters.flaw: You're so busy keeping things fun that you skip the hard conversations.
characters.signature: A huge grin and a yes before anyone's finished asking.
characters.clashReason: they'd stay cheerful even when you really need them to be serious

characters.name: Hollyhock
characters.title: The Open Heart
characters.summary: Warm, curious and honest about how you feel. You give people a chance, but you know when to step back.
description: Like Hollyhock, you grew up with plenty of love. She was raised by eight dads.
You're curious about the world and the people in it. She went off to Wesleyan University as a freshman.
You know where your limits are. When BoJack pushed too hard, Hollyhock told him to give her space.
characters.flaw: You trust people quickly, and it hurts when they let you down.
characters.signature: A long list of questions and your heart on your sleeve.
characters.clashReason: they'd want to talk about how everyone's feeling, right now

characters.name: Judah
characters.title: The Straight Face
characters.summary: Calm, efficient and completely literal. You don't do drama. You do the job.
description: Like Judah, you're quietly reliable. He became a part-owner of VIM, and was later brought back to run it.
You say exactly what you mean. Judah is famously deadpan and struggles with jokes and sarcasm.
Your loyalty runs deeper than it looks. Judah eventually married Princess Carolyn.
characters.flaw: You can come across as cold when you're just being clear.
characters.signature: A spreadsheet, a straight face and zero small talk.
characters.clashReason: they'd take your jokes literally and answer them seriously

questions.text: A friend invites you to a party where you won't know anyone. You...

options.text: Say yes, then cancel an hour before because you're not feeling it
Go, and chat with literally everyone there
Find the one quiet person, and have a deep conversation all night
Bring a strange party game nobody's ever heard of
Make a colour-coded plan, and take on even more
Work through it one task at a time, and still leave on time
Complain that nobody appreciates you, then do the bare minimum
Start wondering whether this job means anything at all

questions.text: A friend tells you about a big personal problem. You...

options.text: Listen, then ask a lot of gentle questions
Nod along, then change the subject when it gets heavy
Suggest three practical next steps
Try to cheer them up with something completely random

questions.text: You've got a whole Sunday with nothing planned. You...

options.text: Wander around and see where the day takes you
Sign up for a class to learn something new
Catch up on work emails, just for an hour (it's never an hour)
Stay in with a book and your own thoughts

questions.text: Someone gives you honest criticism. You...

options.text: Thank them, and write it down
Get defensive, and lie awake replaying it all night
Laugh it off. You can't stay down for long
Argue the point, because you're pretty sure you're right

questions.text: You have a big decision to make. You...

options.text: Research it properly, then decide by the date you set
Go with your gut, and say yes before you can change your mind
Put it off for as long as humanly possible
Decide fast, and deal with the fallout later

questions.text: You get some unexpectedly good news. You...

options.text: Tell everyone you've ever met
Wait for the catch. Good things never last
Call the people you love first
Celebrate in the most ridiculous way you can think of

questions.text: Someone you love keeps letting you down. You...

options.text: Tell them honestly that it hurts, and take a step back
Give them another chance. And another
Write them a long message you never send
Calmly stop counting on them

questions.text: You're asked to plan a friend's birthday. You...

options.text: Book everything weeks ahead, with backups
Throw a huge surprise party with a theme nobody asked for
Come up with a wild idea that somehow works
Admit you're not really a party person, and suggest a small dinner

questions.text: A new neighbour moves in next door. You...

options.text: Bring something over, and make them feel welcome
Introduce yourself briefly, and remember their name
Wave, then feel oddly hurt they didn't come over first
Say hello, and somehow end up hanging out for six hours

questions.text: You're a famous actor, and an old co-star is about to tell the press about something bad you did years ago. You...

options.text: Hire someone to get ahead of the story before it breaks
Tell the truth yourself, in your own words, first
Try to charm your way out of it, and panic when that fails
Hold a cheerful press conference about something else entirely

questions.text: You run a small talent agency, and your biggest client wants to leave. You...

options.text: Pull an all-nighter to win them back
Let them go, and update the client list
Offer them a perk nobody has ever thought of
Tell them you'll miss working with them, and mean it
